mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by > 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening economy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market participants react to the negative economic news.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by > 0.5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where RSAFS declined for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (proxied by INDPRO) by more than 1% within two months signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from increased production and efficiency.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increased by > 1% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending is expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increased by > 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% within three months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy feels the effects of reduced construction activity.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where HOUST decreased by > 10% within three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3%, it signals an environment of high inflation and tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate further rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 3%
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increased by > 0.5% in a month and FEDFUNDS was above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over a quarter signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to grow.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 increased by > 2% over a quarter.
